tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (the-benchmarker/web-frameworks) runs micro-web (the micro-http workspace's framework crate) and actix in one run with public code (rust/micro-web/src/main.rs, rust/micro-web/Cargo.toml, rust/Dockerfile, rust/actix) and stated Rust flags, but no real CPU model (hard-coded cpu_name), so not A. It stays B only because the older-method 2026-09-20 snapshot shows a 1.11-1.17x win; the current 2026-09-24 run shows parity, so the claim is overstated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json, develop commit f673364 (2026-09-24): micro-web 0.3 169,642 / 166,580 / 166,409 req/s at concurrency 64 / 256 / 512 vs actix (actix-web 4.8) 179,203 / 168,270 / 163,415 req/s, i.e. 0.95x / 0.99x / 1.02x (derived from page data). It is slower at c=64 and c=256 and ~2% faster only at c=512. The older-method snapshot on master (commit 0fccb1d, 2026-09-20) shows 135,783 / 113,734 / 112,482 vs 115,638 / 102,329 / 99,835 req/s, i.e. 1.17x / 1.11x / 1.13x (derived from page data).
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks develop-branch run of 2026-09-24 (commit f673364): zrk --closed, a closed loop over keep-alive connections (not wrk), 15 s per concurrency level 64/256/512; the framework container is pinned to cores 0-3 and the load generator to cores 4-15 (.env). Each headline req/s is avg() over the three routes in .env (GET / with empty body, GET /user/0 echoing the id, POST /user with empty body) per .tasks/db.rake, so it is not a single plaintext route. All handlers are hello-world.
corrections.hardware: Undisclosed x86_64 Linux host (Fedora 44 kernel 7.2.6-200.fc44.x86_64), 16 logical CPUs. The cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' (and the memory figure) in data.json are strings hard-coded in .tasks/db.rake, not measured. Server pinned to cores 0-3 (it kept ~3.95 cores busy at ~98.7% saturation per data.json), load generator to cores 4-15.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: micro-web 0.3 (crates.io) on tokio multi-thread, Rust 1.98 (rust:1.98-slim), cargo build --release with opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort (rust/micro-web/Cargo.toml, rust/Dockerfile). Baseline actix-web 4.8: Rust 1.98 (rust:1.98-slim), cargo build --release with opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort (rust/actix/Cargo.toml, rust/Dockerfile).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 29 stars; micro-web crate 12,055 all-time crates.io downloads (109 recent)
corrections.caveats: Very low notability. The shootout measured micro-web 0.3 from crates.io (last published 2025-10-03), not the repo head (e.g. the 2026-08-01 response-write-path optimization). In the current-method 2026-09-24 run it is at parity with actix (0.95x / 0.99x / 1.02x at c=64/256/512); the 1.11-1.17x lead appears only in the superseded-method 2026-09-20 snapshot, and the suite's README says results from different revisions are not comparable. The project's own README makes no speed claim and says it is 'not in this benchmark yet'. Single synthetic hello-world workload (3-route average). Hardware metadata is inconsistent ('M1 Eight-Core Processor' on x86_64, hard-coded).

notes: The numbers belong to the 'micro-web' row (id 3142, website foldright/micro-http) and match to rounding (166,408.52 req/s). The claim picks the only concurrency where micro-web beats actix; at c=64 and c=256 in the same run it is slower, so the verdict is downgrade (tier source still B). Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, 29 stars, last commit 2026-08-01, not a fork, not archived.

Margin over actix is 1.11-1.14x in the 2026-09-24 run but only 1.03-1.05x in the superseded-method 2026-09-20 snapshot, and the suite says revisions are not comparable. Single synthetic hello-world workload. Hardware metadata is inconsistent ('M1 Eight-Core Processor' on x86_64, hard-coded).

notes: Numbers match the 'morojs-engine' row (id 1477, website Moro-JS/engine); it ranks 4th of 387 at c=512 vs actix 20th. benchmark_url pinned to commit f673364 and workload corrected from wrk/plaintext to zrk --closed with a 3-route average. Baseline actix-web 4.8: Rust 1.98 (rust:1.98-slim), cargo build --release with opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort (rust/actix/Cargo.toml, rust/Dockerfile).
corrections.caveats: Node.js V8-addon binding over the already-catalogued uWebSockets C++ core (git submodule); its speed is uWebSockets', so C++ users should use uWebSockets directly. Distinct repo, but not published to the npm registry (installed from GitHub tags). The 2026-09-24 run used plain JS callbacks; the suite switched its app to DeclarativeResponse (answered in C++) after that run (PR #9828), so later numbers are not like-for-like. Run-to-run variation is large: 1.06-1.07x on 2026-09-24, 0.99-1.04x (parity) in the superseded-method 2026-09-20 snapshot, 1.33-1.42x on 2026-09-18 (commit 8ae370a). README says Apache-2.0 applies where explicit notice is given. Single hello-world workload; hardware metadata hard-coded.

notes: Judged a distinct entry, not a known-project duplicate: separate repo and package with its own binding code (src/addon.cpp, *Wrapper.h) and its own independent evidence vs actix, consistent with how bindings such as zsv-ruby and aws-lc-rs were kept; the known_list line for uwebsockets.js comes from this record's wave-5 merge. GitHub reports C++ as the primary language (JS is ~3 KB). Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, 9,161 stars, last commit 2026-09-20, not a fork, not archived.
